## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Ambajātaka* (Ja 344), rendered in English as *The Mangoes*, is a narrative belonging to the Jātaka collection of the late canonical Pali literature [SuttaCentral]. According to the traditional introductory context (*paccuppannavatthu*), the Buddha related the narrative while residing at Jetavana monastery, occasioned by an elder who was charged with keeping watch over ripe mango fruit [SuttaCentral]. The core verse of the story opens with the phrase, “She that did thy mangoes eat” [SuttaCentral]. In V. Fausböll's edition of the Jātaka commentary, the text appears in Volume 3 within the *Catukkanipāta*, where manuscript colophons register it as the fourth tale of its vagga (*ambajātakam catuttham*) [Fausböll 1883].
Care must be taken to distinguish Ja 344 from two other homonymous Jātaka stories bearing the title *Ambajātaka*, namely Ja 124 in the *Ekanipāta* and Ja 474 in the *Paññāsanipāta*. SuttaCentral records no curated external parallels for Ja 344, while listing modern translations across four languages [SuttaCentral]. Automated text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus likewise detects no significant Pali-internal text reuse and no cross-language matches scoring 10 or higher in Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan corpora [DharmaNexus].
